title: First read-only cybersecurity package tranche — upstream evidence

method.github_rest: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo} and GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/latest and GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/tags/{tag} via the GitHub REST API (metadata only)
method.osv: POST https://api.osv.dev/v1/query with package+version (pinned-version check) and package-only (advisory history)
method.pypi: GET https://pypi.org/pypi/checkdmarc/json and /pypi/checkdmarc/6.0.1/json (metadata and wheel digests)
method.license_files: first lines of LICENSE/LICENCE at the pinned release tag for drwetter/testssl.sh and WithSecureLabs/chainsaw
not_performed: no live scan against any host, network, or domain
no CVE database sweep beyond OSV and GitHub security advisories

candidates.name: Syft
candidates.job: Generate a Software Bill of Materials for an owner-selected local directory or filesystem snapshot
candidates.user_story: As the operator, I want an SBOM for a workspace folder or container rootfs tarball so I can see every package and version before I trust or ship it.

license.evidence: GitHub REST /repos/anchore/syft license.spdx_id = Apache-2.0; raw LICENSE at v1.51.1 is the Apache License 2.0

maintenance.release_cadence_note: Frequent tagged releases; v1.51.1 is 18 days old at capture

provenance.note: cosign-style checksum signature pair present; our catalog adds its own sha256 + Ed25519 artifact signature regardless

advisories.pinned_version_note: OSV reports no advisory affecting the pinned version at capture time

history.summary: Credential disclosure in syft when SYFT_ATTEST_PASSWORD environment variable set

advisories.note: Historical advisory themes — credential environment variables and temporary file handling — shape the wrapper rule that no secret env vars are passed to the tool and temp files stay inside the plugin-owned workspace

classification.notes: Reads local files only; outputs an SBOM to stdout or a plugin-owned result path

bounded_input_notes: accepts a workspace-relative directory or a tarball path inside the workspace only
reuses the extension static-scan bounds as runtime defaults: <= 50,000 files, <= 512 MB, <= 10 minutes
does not follow symlinks out of the workspace; special files (devices, FIFOs) are skipped
no network egress in tranche one; catalog and SBOM generation run offline
unverified: runtime behavior on Windows hosts (not tested; excluded from catalog v1 platforms)
upstream source-code quality review (metadata and advisories only)

candidates.name: Grype
candidates.job: Match a local SBOM, directory, or rootfs against vulnerability data and produce a findings report
candidates.user_story: As the operator, I want the packages in my project checked against known vulnerabilities and a severity-ranked report I can act on locally.

maintenance.release_cadence_note: Frequent tagged releases; v0.118.0 is 18 days old at capture

history.summary: Grype has a credential disclosure vulnerability in its JSON output

advisories.note: The JSON output credential-disclosure history reinforces the redaction rule for all scanner output before it reaches chat, logs, or artifacts

classification.notes: Targets are local artifacts; the only network use is the official vulnerability DB refresh, which can be pre-staged for offline mode

manifest_plan.network_allowlist_note: Exact official Anchore DB endpoint hosts must be captured from the pinned binary and written into the manifest for preview before installation.

bounded_input_notes: tranche one scans local directories, SBOM files, or exported rootfs tarballs only — no container socket, no live image pull
DB refresh is a separate bounded network action; offline mode uses a pre-staged DB inside the plugin data directory
findings output is redacted before agent/UI exposure and is stored owner-scoped
unverified: exact pinned DB endpoint hosts for the manifest allowlist (to be captured from the pinned binary during adaptation)
offline DB staging workflow and its size bounds (unimplemented)

candidates.name: OSV-Scanner
candidates.job: Audit project dependency/lockfiles against OSV vulnerability data
candidates.user_story: As the operator, I want my lockfiles checked against OSV so I know which dependencies need an update and can see the advisory links.

maintenance.release_cadence_note: Very active; v2.6.0 published on the capture date

provenance.note: multiple.intoto.jsonl SLSA provenance asset plus SHA256SUMS

advisories.note: No OSV or repository advisories observed at capture time

classification.notes: Reads lockfiles and source manifests; queries api.osv.dev unless an offline database is provided

manifest_plan.network_allowlist_note: The OSV API endpoint is confirmed; the official offline-database source host must be captured from the pinned binary during adaptation.

bounded_input_notes: scans workspace-relative manifests and lockfiles only
network queries are advisory lookups of package coordinates — never target probes
offline mode must be supported because the host may be air-gapped

candidates.name: Gitleaks
candidates.job: Scan a local repository or directory for committed secrets without leaving the host
candidates.user_story: As the operator, I want to check a repo for committed credentials before I share it, and see file/line locations without exposing the secret values in chat.

maintenance.release_cadence_note: Active repository; v8.30.1 is the latest tag at capture (March 2026) with commits through September 2026

provenance.note: Checksums only; our catalog signing supplies the publish-time provenance

advisories.note: No OSV or repository advisories observed at capture time

classification.notes: Highest data-sensitivity candidate: findings can contain live credentials, so output redaction and owner-scoped storage are mandatory controls

bounded_input_notes: scans a workspace-relative git checkout or directory
secret values are redacted in every agent-visible, logged, or stored preview; raw values are never written to shared artifacts
findings are owner-scoped with an explicit retention/removal path
no network egress; no git history rewriting and no remediation actions
unverified: the exact redaction coverage of every gitleaks rule type against our redactor (fixture tests required during adaptation)

candidates.name: checkdmarc
candidates.job: Inspect SPF, DMARC, DKIM, and MX posture for an owner-specified domain over DNS-over-HTTPS
candidates.user_story: As the operator, I want a bounded check of my own domain's email-authentication records so I can find missing or misconfigured SPF/DMARC entries.

license.evidence: GitHub REST license.spdx_id = Apache-2.0; PyPI license_expression = Apache-2.0

maintenance.release_cadence_note: Small but active; 6.0.1 published 10 days before capture

provenance.checksums_asset: PyPI sha256 digests for the wheel and sdist recorded in the PyPI metadata
provenance.note: PyPI attestation availability was not checked; dependency wheels must be pinned with hashes during adaptation

dependencies.packaging_note: Python dependency tree is the largest in the tranche; adaptation must vendor hash-pinned wheels and run a dependency audit

advisories.note: The dependency tree, not checkdmarc itself, is the CVE surface; audit pinned wheels during adaptation

classification.notes: DNS lookups are bounded to operator-named domains over DoH; enumeration or bulk domain lists are excluded by design

manifest_plan.network_allowlist_note: DNS-over-HTTPS resolver endpoints only; the exact endpoints must be selected and written into the manifest for preview before installation.
host_dependencies: Python 3.10+ runtime provided by the plugin package; no host package installation

bounded_input_notes: one operator-named domain per invocation; no zone transfers, no wildcard sweeps, no domain lists
DNS transport restricted to DNS-over-HTTPS endpoints in the manifest network allowlist so the external effect is visible before install
results carry record contents only and are owner-scoped
no email sending, no mailbox access, no SMTP probing
unverified: pure-DNS/UDP transport is not representable in the manifest network allowlist; DoH-only is a required adaptation constraint

candidates.name: CycloneDX CLI
candidates.job: Validate, merge, diff, and convert CycloneDX SBOMs into readable report formats
candidates.user_story: As the operator, I want the SBOMs I already own validated and merged into one report so I can hand a consistent inventory to another tool or person.

maintenance.release_cadence_note: Maintained; v0.33.1 published ~7 weeks before capture

provenance.note: Release assets are bare binaries without checksums; publish-time provenance comes only from the signed catalog artifact. This is the weakest upstream provenance in the tranche and is called out for Leo.

advisories.pinned_version_osv_query: NuGet CycloneDX.Cli at a matching version could not be resolved exactly; OSV history query for the module returned 0
advisories.note: No advisories observed; NuGet ecosystem/version mapping is approximate and marked unverified

classification.notes: Operates on SBOM files the operator already owns; writes new report files but never mutates inputs in place

bounded_input_notes: reads SBOM files inside the workspace and writes merged/report output to a plugin-owned result path
file size and element count bounds reuse the extension static-scan bounds
no schema fetching from the network at runtime; schemas are pinned in the package
unverified: exact NuGet package identity for OSV version matching
upstream release checksum/signature absence risk acceptance (requires catalog signing only)

candidates.name: Chainsaw
candidates.job: Search Windows event logs (EVTX) and other forensic artifacts against Sigma rules locally
candidates.user_story: As the operator, I want to hunt through exported Windows event logs on this machine with Sigma rules and get a findings report.
candidates.condition: Approve only if the plugin package ships the upstream GPL-3.0 LICENCE and a pinned source offer; GPL-3.0 is compatible with this AGPL-3.0-or-later project at the aggregate/plugin boundary.

license.evidence: GitHub REST license.spdx_id = GPL-3.0; raw LICENCE at v2.16.5 is the GNU GPL version 3 text

maintenance.release_cadence_note: Steady releases; v2.16.5 published ~3 weeks before capture

provenance.note: No release checksums or signatures; publish-time provenance comes from the signed catalog artifact

advisories.note: No OSV or repository advisories observed at capture time

classification.notes: Offline forensic log search; no live system access, no memory acquisition, no endpoint agent

bounded_input_notes: reads exported log/artifact files inside the workspace only
Sigma rule packs are pinned in the package; no runtime rule downloads
bounds and redaction reuse the static-scan limits
unverified: rule pack licensing for bundled Sigma rules (Sigma rules are typically DRL; to be audited during adaptation)

candidates.name: testssl.sh
candidates.job: Audit the TLS configuration of one operator-owned host:port
candidates.user_story: As the operator, I want a configuration audit of one of my own services' TLS endpoint so I can fix weak protocols or cipher settings.
candidates.condition: Approve only with a single explicit host:port per invocation, an operator target-ownership attestation, rate limits, and GPL-2.0-or-later compliance packaging. Unrestricted or list-based scanning stays excluded.

license.evidence: GitHub REST license key gpl-2.0; raw LICENSE at v3.2.4 contains the GPLv2 text with the 'any later version' option, so GPL-3.0/AGPL-3.0 compatibility applies

maintenance.release_cadence_note: Very active; default branch is 3.3dev, stable v3.2.4 from July 2026

windows: not supported upstream in tranche one
platforms.source: project README/platform notes; no release binary assets

provenance.note: Source-only release; the plugin package must pin the tag and ship the script plus LICENSE, with catalog-level signing

advisories.pinned_version_osv_query: not a package ecosystem; no OSV entry
advisories.note: Shell/openssl toolchain CVEs are the real surface; host openssl version matters and is outside upstream control

classification.notes: TLS handshake probing has a large per-target footprint; bounded to one named host:port and gated by ownership attestation

manifest_plan.network_allowlist_note: The host:port target is not expressible in the https URL allowlist; the single-target ownership gate must live in the wrapper and the target confirmation must be visible in the plan preview.
host_dependencies: openssl (host-provided, version recorded at install preview)

bounded_input_notes: exactly one host:port per invocation, resolved to one address, no ranges/CIDR/lists
operator attestation that the target is owned or authorized
rate limit and timeout caps per run
no exploitation, no certificate forging, no connection flooding
unverified: whether the manifest network boundary can express a host:port target (evidence suggests only https URLs are expressible; adaptation may require the ownership gate in the wrapper instead)
